Definition: from G73; to struggle, literally (to compete for a prize), figuratively (to contend with an adversary), or genitive case (to endeavor to accomplish something):--fight, labor fervently, strive.
BiblicalUsage: Agonizomai is to struggle — to compete for a prize, to contend with an adversary, to labour fervently. Jesus says to strive to enter the narrow gate; He says His servants would fight if His kingdom were of this world; Paul says every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things; and he commends Epaphras, who laboured fervently in prayer. The word covers the race, the fight, and the prayer closet — all of them a struggle.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word is the call to take the Christian life seriously. The gate is narrow, the prize is real, and the striving is not anxiety but devotion — a life that fights, runs, and prays like it means it, because it does.
